This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management all in one place, no matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour. Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman. More than 250,000 students around France took to the streets of major cities yesterday to continue to press their demands for better conditions at school. NPR's Eleanor Beersley reports.
Paris's Place de la République was packed with high schoolers who sang the Marseillaise and chanted revolutionary slogans. There were also parents and teachers. All say more needs to be spent on education.
Even kids from well-off neighborhoods are taking part in the movement out of solidarity for those in the poor suburbs and rural areas where schools are not as tended to.
Critics say the government spent too long ignoring the protests and then treated them as a security problem. Protesters say a strong and egalitarian education system is at the heart of France's meritocracy and democracy.
France has a huge deficit and the government is looking for places to cut, not spend. There are fears the protests, on top of rising energy prices, could lead to further social disruption.
Today is the third anniversary of the Hamas-led attack on Israel. It killed about 1,200 people. Israel launched the war on Gaza the following day. More than 74,000 people there have been killed.
Cornell University has chosen an independent investigator to examine how it handled allegations of a gang rape two years ago.
The university named former U.S. Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates as the investigator. Cornell has been criticized for failing to properly punish the men accused of the rape, and B.S. Jacqueline Diaz reports.
Cornell says its university police thoroughly examined the case and the school held its own investigation, which resulted in suspensions with two students expelled.
The university says it wants Yates to examine the school's policy on how it prevents and responds to sexual harassment, assault, and misconduct on campus.
And Pierre's Jacqueline Diaz reporting. The Walt Disney Company has argued in court that the Trump administration is violating its First Amendment rights. The focus is on eight local ABC TV stations owned by Disney.
As David Foconflick reports, the FCC launched early reviews for the station's licenses.
FCC Chief Brendan Carr didn't attend the hearing, but he loomed large over it. President Trump has blasted ABC repeatedly for its content and coverage, and Carr has echoed him.
Disney's attorney said the very threat that those licenses could be taken away has chilled ABC's free speech.
Its attorney said ABC News carried a Trump White House address in July on its streaming service only because it feared retaliation if it didn't.
The U.S. Justice Department's lawyers argued the dispute should be resolved through a bureaucratic appeal process, not the district court.
And the government said the review of the station's licenses was needed to get more information about Disney's diversity initiatives. The judge sounded dubious about that claim.
This is NPR.
This year's Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded to two scientists for their work on mirror images in molecules. Henri B. Kagan and Kenzo Soai have discovered ways to show mirror images in chemical reactions.
This has been critical for investors who are working to create new medications.
Obesity rates in children and adolescents have quadrupled to more than 170 million people since 1990. NPR's Gabriela Emmanuel reports on the World Health Organization's release of its first guidelines on how to treat that age group.
For children under the age of 10 who are obese, the WHO is emphasizing dietary changes and physical activity. They are not recommending surgery or weight loss medications like GLP-1 for children.
Zeus Maria de Regil is with the WHO.
There is not enough evidence that trials are starting. The medications that have been tested are not proven.
She says they are also considering the long-term effect in cost of medications as well as the long-term cost of obesity, which is estimated to be trillions of dollars each year worldwide. Gabriela Emmanuel, NPR News.
Miami-nominated R&B singer Freddie Jackson has died at the age of 70, according to a family statement. Recently, he revealed he had kidney disease. Jackson was famous for songs such as "Rock Me Tonight" and "You Are My Lady."
The National Hurricane Center says Tropical Storm Iseiz has formed in the Gulf of Mexico. It could be a significant hurricane when it reaches shore. This is NPR.
